headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can feed sensitive context into Plandex’s write-capable coding workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context, and Plandex can read project files and stdin/stdout in a coding workflow. If Perplexity’s output is copied into Plandex or stored in a shared workspace, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted or saved into a Plandex plan or project file
IF Plandex is run on content originating from Perplexity without provenance tagging
mitigations: Use a separate scratch file for Perplexity outputs
Require manual review before Plandex consumes any copied text
Prefix imported text with a non-executable delimiter
Disable auto-apply while testing the pair
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and sends queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context to its backend, while Plandex reads local project files and can write changes. If sensitive source code or documents are placed in the shared workflow, Perplexity may ingest them and transmit them to a third-party service. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default usage.
conditions: IF source code or confidential documents are copied into Perplexity prompts or uploads
IF Plandex project files contain secrets and are summarized by Perplexity
mitigations: Do not send secrets or proprietary code to Perplexity
Use redacted excerpts instead of full files
Keep Plandex projects and Perplexity sessions in separate workspaces
Review uploaded-document lists before submitting
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on copied content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Perplexity can browse and handle uploaded files but does not write the host filesystem. The overlap is not a direct write-write collision, yet both can touch the same project artifacts if the operator bridges them. That creates a moderate conflict risk, especially around staged code changes.
conditions: IF Perplexity-derived edits are applied to the same git working tree Plandex is modifying
IF both agents are allowed to operate on the same project directory
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access at a time
Keep Perplexity read-only with respect to project artifacts
Commit or stash before handing work between agents
Use separate branches for each agent
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from live web search, and Plandex is a planner that stages and applies code changes. If Plandex treats Perplexity’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated answer can cascade into incorrect code or commits. The pair therefore has a default pathway from generated facts to downstream action without built-in verification.
conditions: IF Plandex uses Perplexity answers as source-of-truth without independent checks
IF Perplexity output is converted into plan steps or code edits
mitigations: Require a second source before acting on Perplexity claims
Have Plandex mark imported facts as untrusted
Review staged diffs before apply
Limit auto-apply mode during cross-tool workflows
requires-engineering: add citation verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and handles uploaded documents and browsing context, while Plandex handles source code and may send data to a model provider or Plandex Cloud. If regulated data or proprietary code is moved between them, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents or code are processed in both tools
IF organizational policy requires identical retention or residency controls across vendors
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity sessions
Confirm Plandex backend residency before use
Avoid uploading confidential code to vendor-hosted services
Document retention expectations for both tools
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and residency review
